headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap from Claude Code; LlamaFactory is inert, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but write-conflict and cascading-error risks remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can ingest repo files and user-provided directories, so malicious content in shared files could influence it. LlamaFactory has no filesystem, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so there is no automatic back-channel from B into A. The pathway exists only through manual file handoff, making blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into files that A reads, A may follow injected instructions.
mitigations: Review shared files before opening them in A.
Keep B outputs in a separate directory.
Use a plain-text allowlist for files A may read.
Strip instructions from any copied artifacts before handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and cwd files, while LlamaFactory exposes no file or network surfaces. Because B cannot read files or call APIs, there is no direct exfiltration path from A into B; leakage is limited to manual transfer of content by the operator.
conditions: IF the operator pastes A's outputs into B's training or support workflow, sensitive code or secrets may be copied out.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets into B.
Redact credentials before sharing outputs.
Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Use a scrubber for logs and transcripts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; LlamaFactory has no write or network capabilities. The pair still conflicts because A can mutate the shared filesystem and git state that B may later consume indirectly, and the profile explicitly says shared state is via filesystem and git only. That makes concurrent writes dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or cwd, A can overwrite files or git state that downstream workflows rely on.
mitigations: Run A and B in separate directories.
Serialize access to the repo.
Disable A's write access for read-only tasks.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Use a lock file around git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code, patches, and shell actions that may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows, while LlamaFactory is not runnable and has no action-taking authority. The main risk is A's output being reused without verification; B does not independently validate A, so errors can cascade into later human or tool actions.
conditions: IF A's generated patch or command is copied into a deployment or commit step without review, an error can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before applying patches.
Diff A's output against the intended change.
Run tests before commit.
Keep B out of the execution path for A's commands.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data flow is evidenced between the pair. Claude Code touches source code and git history, but LlamaFactory exposes no file, network, or OAuth surfaces and no data classes touched, so there is no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually introduced into either agent's workspace, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Document any data-class changes.
Review retention settings before use.
